title: Show HN: Unspin – live per-step progress for Claude Code's shell commands

item.title: Show HN: Unspin – live per-step progress for Claude Code's shell commands

sources.text:
unspin
See what your coding agent's shell commands are doing, instead of a spinner.
When Claude Code runs a long shell command, you get the command and a spinner until it ends. Is it installing? On the fourth of fifty downloads? Stuck? You can't tell. unspin teaches the agent to mark the steps of its batched commands as it goes, and shows them live. Claude Code's own spinner names the step that is running, and a block above the prompt lists every step with a progress bar, its time and an ETA.
✻ Baking · building image 37/72, eta 33s… (1m 12s · ↓ 2.1k tokens)
▶ Ship the release  step 4/6 · 1m14s
✔ linting 1.2s
✘ running tests 120/120 — 1 of 120 failed 23s
· test_88.py is a known flake, carrying on
⠴ building image 35s  ━━━━━───── 37/72 · eta 33s · layer sha256:ab12cd34ef56
Install
In Claude Code, install the plugin. There is nothing to configure.
/plugin marketplace add nkyriazis/unspin
/plugin install unspin@unspin
Restart Claude Code, then ask Claude to run the
unspin demo
command.
Prefer the flow under your status line, or still on Claude Code before 2.1.287? Use the installer instead. It backs up
settings.json
before changing it.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/unspin/main/install.sh
|
bash
More ways to install
covers both at once, other agents and installing from a clone.
Everyday use
Tell Claude once, at the start of a session.
use unspin from now on
From then on, when it batches several steps into one command or starts something long, such as a build, a test run, a loop over files or a wait for a server, it marks the steps and you watch them as they go. A hook reminds it when it forgets. A long job can also run in the background with its progress in view.
To have this in every session without asking, add a line like this to
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
.
Use the unspin skill for batched and long-running shell commands, so I can see their steps and progress live.
What the agent writes
The skill gives Claude a few shell functions. A typical command looks like this.
source
"
${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}
/unspin.sh
"
flow
"
Ship the release
"
6
run -q
"
installing dependencies
"
npm ci
flow_each -j 4
"
optimizing images
"
assets/
*
.png -- optipng -quiet {}
run -p
"
building
"
ninja -C build
run
"
unit tests
"
npm
test
&
run
"
lint
"
npm run lint
&
wait
flow_wait -t 60
"
waiting for the preview
"
-- curl -sf localhost:3000/health
Call
What it does
flow "Title" [N]
Starts a flow of N steps
step "msg"
,
ok
,
fail
,
note "msg"
Open a step, close it, or add a note
run "msg" cmd…
A step around one command, closed by its exit status.
-l
shows its latest output line,
-p
reads counts like
[3/10]
from it,
-q
keeps the output in a log and prints only the tail if it fails
progress N [TOTAL] ["label"]
Moves the bar. Counts can carry units (
1.2G/4G
) or be percentages
flow_each [-j N] "msg" items… -- cmd {}
A loop with one bar, the current item and a failure tally, N at a time
flow_wait [-t SECS] "msg" -- cmd…
Retries until cmd succeeds, with a bar for the time
cmd | flow_lines [-p]
Counts output lines as progress, or reads counts from them
Jobs started with
&
each get their own row. The
skill
has the details the agent reads.
Where it shows
Where
How
Claude Code's spinner, and the band above the prompt
the plugin
Under your Claude Code status line
unspin setup
, which the installer runs
Your own status line script
unspin block "$session_id"
prints the block, or nothing
ccstatusline and other status line builders
a custom command running
unspin statusline --line
A second terminal or a tmux pane
unspin watch
The tmux status bar
set -g status-right '#(unspin tmux)'
and
set -g status-interval 1
Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Goose, Cline, Cursor, Amp
each step is also printed to the command's stderr, which these agents show
How it works
The helper appends one line per event to a file for the agent session, in
$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/unspin
or
/tmp/unspin-<uid>
. The plugin reads that file twice a second and the status line once a second, and both draw it. No daemon runs and nothing goes over the network. The helper writes to that file and not to stdout, so the agent still reads the command's own output.
Each event is a plain line of text, so anything that can append to a file can report progress. A Python loop, a Makefile and a hand-typed
echo
all work. The format is in
docs/protocol.md
.
A step remembers the process that opened it. If that process dies before closing the step (you pressed Esc, the shell was killed), the step shows as interrupted instead of spinning forever. Steps that are running or have failed stay in view when later steps would push them out. A short reminder reaches Claude when it writes a batched command without the helper, at most once every five minutes. When you send your next prompt the finished flow is put away.
Configuration
Set these in the environment, or under
env
in Claude Code's
settings.json
.
Variable
Default
Effect
UNSPIN_ROWS
4
Steps shown under the header
UNSPIN_SPINNER
1
0
keeps the plugin out of the spinner
UNSPIN_BAND
1
0
keeps the plugin out of the band above the prompt
UNSPIN_NUDGE
1
0
stops the reminder to instrument batched commands
UNSPIN_ECHO
auto
1
also writes each step to stderr,
0
never does. Auto turns it on in agents without a live status line
UNSPIN_ASCII
0
1
draws with plain ASCII
NO_COLOR
Turns color off in the status line
UNSPIN_DIR
Where flow files go
Works with
bash 3.2 (the one macOS ships) to 5.3, and zsh. gawk, mawk, busybox awk and BSD awk. Linux and macOS. The test suite runs the helper under each of these shells and the status line renderer under each of these awks, and the plugin's mod under Claude Code's own test kit.
Troubleshooting
unspin doctor
checks the install and says what to fix.
If the plugin is installed but nothing shows in the spinner or above the prompt, mods may be off for your account or organization.
claude --debug
logs why a mod did not load. The status line works either way, so until that changes, add it next to the plugin as in
More ways to install
.
More ways to install
Both places.
With the plugin installed, run the installer with
--statusline
. It then adds only the status line.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nkyriazis/unspin/main/install.sh
|
bash -s -- --statusline
Other agents.
npx skills add nkyriazis/unspin
installs the skill for Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Cursor, Goose and the other agents
skills
knows about.
Where it shows
says what you see in each.
From a clone.
git clone https://github.com/nkyriazis/unspin && unspin/install.sh
installs that working copy.
Uninstall
The plugin goes with
/plugin uninstall unspin@unspin
. The installer's setup goes with
unspin uninstall
, which restores your status line and hooks, and then
rm -rf ~/.local/share/unspin
removes the files.

comments.text:
When you enable it does two things: 
 - it biases the model to act in compounds, a bit more, i.e. get more done in less tool uses
 - it pushes for the right amount of feedback while waiting, on the spinner or at the status bar
I know that lately watching claude work isn't a thing, but, when it's not that time...
